# Burnly v0.1.33

Adds DeepSeek Harness collection, makes tray model rows attribution-truthful when two agents share a model label, and fixes the Linux AppImage so it starts on older distributions instead of requiring glibc 2.38 or newer.

## Highlights

- **Linux AppImage portability.** The AppImage previously required `GLIBC_2.38`/`GLIBC_2.39`, so it refused to start on Ubuntu 22.04 and other older-but-supported distributions. Linux artifacts are now built against the oldest still-supported Ubuntu LTS (glibc 2.35), and `.DirIcon` is a relative symlink rather than an absolute path into the build machine. This is also what the AppImageHub catalog requires, so Burnly can be listed there.
- **DeepSeek Harness source (experimental).** Burnly now discovers a local DeepSeek Harness installation at `~/.dsh` and reads its session format 4 event logs under `sessions/`, collecting daily and session usage from assistant settlements, including subagent sessions. Unsupported newer or older session generations fail closed or mark the refresh partial rather than guessing. Cost is Burnly-calculated from the embedded models.dev pricing snapshot when the route model is priced; every currently observed DSH route is unpriced, so cost is reported as unavailable rather than estimated. See `docs/engineering/known-limitations.md`.
- **Tray model rows split by agent.** When two agents used the same model label, the tray merged them into a single `Multiple agents` row with a combined total and no way to see the split. Rows are now grouped by both model label and source, so each row resolves to exactly one agent with its own token total, and the split rows sum to the previously merged total. Trend baselines compare like with like: a row's trend is measured against yesterday's tokens for the same model and the same agent, and a pair that did not exist yesterday reads `new today` instead of inheriting a merged baseline.

## Privacy

Burnly continues to read usage-only metadata. It selects model identity, token
counters, and generation timestamps; it never reads prompt text, response
content, tool invocations, project paths, or sensitive credentials.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.33/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.33 sh
```

The AppImage now runs on Ubuntu 22.04 and newer.

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.33-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is not Authenticode-signed. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the
official GitHub release and verify the published `SHA256SUMS`. Tauri updater
artifacts remain cryptographically signed.

### macOS Preview

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-macos.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.33/install-macos.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.33 sh
```

Manual `.dmg` installation is also available:

```text
burnly-v0.1.33-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.33-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

The macOS preview is unsigned and not notarized. If Gatekeeper blocks the
downloaded app, clear quarantine once after copying it to Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Verification

This release was verified with the full local gates (119 frontend tests, 792 Rust
tests). The AppImage changes were verified against the previous release artifact:
the new checks fail on `v0.1.32` with `GLIBC_2.39` and report its absolute
`.DirIcon` target, a rebuilt artifact carries a relative `.DirIcon`, and the
catalog's own `appdir-lint.sh` reports no fatal issues while
`desktop-file-validate` passes. The Linux AppImage smoke test now fails any
release whose bundled binaries need a symbol version above glibc 2.35.

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`, GitHub build provenance, signed updater
artifacts, `latest.json`, and the `latest-linux.json` compatibility alias.
